headline: Minnesotans used to split their tickets. Political polarization changed that pattern.
dek: Amy Klobuchar is a uniquely popular politician. We wanted to know if that two-decade streak of statewide support would change when she ran for governor. What started as a live-updating, internal-only visual turned into a story, tracking counties won by a Republican for senate and Klobuchar for governor. Written and designed by me, this story explores how increasing metro populations and political polarization have reduced overall split tickets.

headline: What's on my ballot for the 2026 Minnesota midterms?
dek: For the midterms, we wanted to reinvision a more useful and accessible voter guide. After several months of ideating, I pitched joining it with our ballot finder and adding an onboarding process for the kinds of decisions voters might make when deciding who to vote for. I worked with a dozen reporters, photographers, editors and designers to come up with a new resource for voters built off of original reporting, campaign finance disclosures and clear breakdowns of candidate issues.

headline: Vance Boelter's 43 hours on the run
dek: A team of investigative reporters spent a year trying to understand the scope of the biggest manhunt in state history, tracking every step with public records requests. My task was to translate documents into visual data to answer two questions for our audience: Where was the suspect during the 43 hours? And why did it take so long for multiple law enforcement agencies to find him?

headline: What does the new WNBA CBA mean for the Lynx?
dek: Salaries for players in the WNBA skyrocketed after a contentious 16 months and a marathon week of closed-door negotiations over a new collective bargaining agreement in 2026. For the Lynx’s hometown newspaper, I reported, charted and designed this story on how negotiations could impact the salaries of the 2026 roster.
alt: Animated gif showing 9 faceted bar charts, animating an increased 2026 salary over a 2025 salary

headline: In Lake Placid, Jessie Diggins’ swan song
dek: How does one visualize the career of America's greatest cross-country skier? I built a scrolly tracker, sized proportionally to the total (solo) kilometers Diggins has skied professionally, assembled with data from her FIS page. The more than 4,000 kilometers she skied doesn't mean much without context, so we added little anchors to help orient a Minnesota audience in that distance. And, even though it's not about the medals – Diggins' words – she has a lot of them! As you scroll, you can see just how many she accumulated throughout her career.

headline: Lindsey Vonn’s career in five mountains (and one hill)
dek: Lindsey Vonn is a dominant alpine skier – and a proud Minnesotan export. I designed this piece from Jake Steinberg to explore the mountains that defined her career in the leadup to her final (we think?) Olympics.

headline: From the Gridiron to the Met Gala
dek: They say you can spot Justin Jefferson's chains from the nosebleeds at US Bank stadium. While that isn't true (I tried), it is true that the wide receiver has style. I collaborated with Vikings reporter Emily Leiker to dissect some of Jefferson's most iconic outfits.

headline: How does ranked-choice voting work?
dek: I joined the ranks of designers explaining how Minneapolis municipal elections use ranked choice voting to select City Council, Park Board and mayor. The last municipal election with a strong possibility of an incumbent being unseated was 2017, so I used it as an example of what might happen on election night.

headline: A guide to the 2025 Minneapolis city election
dek: I designed the guide for Minneapolis' 2025 municipal election, which presented answers to key questions from almost everyone running. My favorite part? The homemade navigable map component to help readers orient which ward/park district they were in.

headline: Every State Fair Grandstand performance, visualized
dek: Before Labor Day, the state’s hottest club is the Minnesota State Fair Grandstand. I wanted to know what we could learn from 50 years worth of booking data – what artists get picked? When and why? I broke the data down by genre, gender and by how "relevant" an artist is. Spoiler: There’s a lot of old dudes.

headline: Knee-high by Fourth of July: What grows in Minnesota and why
dek: There are 19.2 million acres of cropland in this state, and most of that cropland is devoted to corn and soybean. But how did Minnesota become such a corn and soy heavy state? Brooks Johnson and I found out by getting friendly with the USDA CDL and the charting library Layercake.
